title: interview-guide template variables
description: Values for templates/interview-guide.md.j2 and templates/interview-guide.html.j2. Generated by tpl-jinja from interview-guide.md; `description` on each property is the question put to the author.

interviewer.title: Interviewer
interviewer.description: Who runs the session. Leading questions are personal habits - naming the interviewer is what makes the neutrality review at the end of this guide possible at all.

objective_2.title: Objective 2
objective_2.description: 2. From section 'Research Objectives (what we need to learn)'.

project_name.description: The project these interviews feed. Sessions get reused across projects and misattributed six months later; the name is what keeps a quote tied to the question it answered.

research_objective_one.title: Research objective one
research_objective_one.description: The first thing you need to learn, phrased so an answer could disappoint you. If no possible response would change your plan, you are booking sessions to confirm something.

research_topic.title: Research topic
research_topic.description: What you are researching, in the participant's language. They hear this sentence in the first ten seconds and decide from it what kind of answers you want - so keep your product out of it.

session_minutes.title: Session minutes
session_minutes.description: How long you tell the participant it will take. Say the true number; running over is the fastest way to lose the last ten minutes, which is where people stop performing.

warmup_activity.title: Warmup activity
warmup_activity.description: The routine activity you ask them to describe first - "how you usually plan your week". Ordinary and specific, to get them narrating rather than opining before the real questions.
